Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Bitnomial is building the next generation US-based global derivatives exchange, starting with digital assets and progressively expanding to encompass a full spectrum of commodities worldwide. Bitnomial operates a US CFTC regulated exchange (DCM), clearinghouse (DCO), and brokerage (FCM). It offers a range of crypto-settled derivatives, including futures, options, and a suite of live perpetual futures, used by brokers, hedge funds, institutions, and trading firms around the world.

Bitnomial's exchange, clearinghouse, and brokerage systems are written largely in Haskell. In this role you will build the services and data models that record every order, fill, and settlement at a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, with the database as a first-class part of the design. You will build features across these systems and design the schema, queries, and migrations behind them.

 

The opportunity

  • Improve build and release pipelines in GitHub Actions: caching, parallelism, pinned toolchains, and required tests and scans before production

  • Manage AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform, and run services as containers on Nomad

  • Build deployment tooling with health checks and automated rollback, and make deploys safe around market sessions

  • Add metrics and alerts to the services you build, so you can see whether a deploy worked

  • Monitor systems, respond to alerts, and support daily operations such as settlement cycles

  • Fix the cause of production issues and write down what you learned

  • Build, test, and ship well-reviewed features and fixes in our services across the exchange, clearinghouse, and brokerage. Most of the code is Haskell

  • Understand the order, trade, clearing, and settlement flows end to end

 

What you bring

  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipelines, such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI

  • Production experience with AWS and Docker, and infrastructure as code with Terraform

  • Strong Linux and scripting skills (Bash, Python, or similar)

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with a functional or strongly typed programming language such as Haskell, Rust, or C++

  • Solid computer science fundamentals, including distributed systems: failure modes, retries and idempotency, consistency, and how to observe them across services

  • Willingness to take part in on-call and operational shifts

  • Care and rigor with code that moves money

  • Good judgment with AI tools. You use them to work faster, and you read, test, and understand what they produce before you ship it

  • A habit of asking why before changing something

  • Sound judgment under pressure, with a calm and methodical approach when production is live

  • Collaboration across engineering, operations, risk, and compliance, with a habit of documenting

 

Nice to haves

  • Financial knowledge or experience in trading, markets, or financial services

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience

  • Experience with Nomad or Kubernetes

  • Experience with Nix, Ansible, Vault, or Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki

  • Haskell experience

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

About Bullish

Bullish is an institutionally focused global digital asset platform that provides market infrastructure and information services. These include: Bullish Exchange – a regulated and institutionally focused digital assets spot and derivatives exchange, integrating a high-performance central limit order book matching engine with automated market making to provide deep and predictable liquidity. Bullish Exchange is regulated in Germany, Hong Kong, and Gibraltar. CoinDesk Indices – a collection of tradable proprietary and single-asset benchmarks and indices that track the performance of digital assets for global institutions in the digital assets and traditional finance industries. CoinDesk Data - a broad suite of digital assets market data and analytics, providing real-time insights into prices, trends, and market dynamics. CoinDesk Insights – a digital asset media and events provider and operator of Coindesk.com, a digital media platform that covers news and insights about digital assets, the underlying markets, policy, and blockchain technology.

Reports to:

Director, Product Management, CoinDesk

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager, Growth to do three things: help us win big with our new subscription business, help us build a truly great mobile app, and be exceptional at building with Claude and other AI tools. You'll drive audience and subscription growth across CoinDesk Media and be a genuine right hand to the Director of Product in shaping where our products go next.


You'll own CoinDesk's growth funnel end to end: how people discover our journalism, activate, build a daily habit, and choose to pay, across the web and the CoinDesk mobile app. With our new subscription product launching, your north star is simple: more readers, more engaged readers, and more of them converting to and staying as paying subscribers.


You'll be deeply data-driven, using Amplitude to understand behavior and running a high-velocity experimentation program that shapes the roadmap. You'll find the growth levers across our news and editorial experience, video, podcasts, newsletters, research and live crypto and stock price data.


This is a builder's role. Product managers at CoinDesk write and release code to production. You'll use AI coding agents to prototype, build, and ship fixes, experiments, and features through our normal pull-request review and CI, alongside engineering. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be at home in a codebase, and you need the keenness, aptitude, and drive to use AI to get far more done than a traditional PM.


What You'll Do:

  • Own the growth model and funnel metrics across web and mobile: acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, and subscription conversion. Set the targets and be accountable for moving them.
  • Lead the launch and growth of our subscription product: paywall and metering strategy, pricing and packaging experiments, offer testing, checkout, onboarding, and the retention and win-back journeys that make a membership business work.
  • Own the CoinDesk mobile app (iOS and Android) as a growth channel: roadmap, release cadence, App Store and Google Play presence and ratings, push notifications, and app-native engagement. Make the app a first-class subscription channel, including in-app purchase and cross-platform entitlements.
  • Run a high-tempo experimentation program: form hypotheses, size tests, prioritize the backlog by expected impact, and use Amplitude funnels, cohorts, and retention curves to decide what ships next.
  • Build growth loops that turn one-time readers into habitual ones: SEO, social distribution, newsletter and push re-engagement, and sharing and referral.
  • Build and ship yourself. Use AI coding agents to write and release production code for experiments, UI changes, and internal tools across our web, mobile, and CMS (Sanity) codebases, working through pull-request review and CI.
  • Use AI to multiply your output across the whole job, from research synthesis and specs to analysis and automating your own workflows, and raise the bar for how the wider team uses it.
  • Work across editorial, design, engineering, marketing, and commercial to deliver one cohesive, high-quality experience, partnering with marketing on lifecycle journeys (HubSpot) triggered by product behavior.

What You Have:

  • 6+ years of product management experience on consumer, audience-facing digital products, including at least 3 years in a growth product manager role or on a growth team, owning funnel metrics such as activation, conversion, or retention.
  • Direct experience building and growing subscription or membership products, ideally including launching a subscription or paywall from the ground up: conversion, paywalls, retention, and lifetime value. 
  • Strong experimentation rigor: sample sizing, statistical significance, guardrail metrics, and holdouts, plus the judgment to know when a result is misleading or traffic is too thin to test.
  • Fluency in Amplitude or a comparable product analytics tool. You build your own funnels, cohorts, and retention analyses without waiting on an analyst.
  • Experience owning a consumer mobile app (iOS and/or Android), including app store releases, push notifications, and mobile monetization.
  • Hands-on, demonstrated use of AI to build. You've shipped working software or tools with AI coding agents and can walk us through what you built.
  • Comfortable working in a codebase: git, pull requests, running an app locally, and discussing APIs, data models, and platform trade-offs with engineers.
  • Exceptional keenness, aptitude, and drive. You pick up new tools quickly, ship without waiting to be asked, and own outcomes end to end.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration and high emotional intelligence, able to communicate clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • Comfortable in a dynamic, distributed organization where priorities can change frequently.

Bonus Points:

  • Mobile growth experience: app store optimization and in-app paywalls.
  • Experience in media, journalism, or other engagement-driven businesses.
  • Familiarity with headless CMS (Sanity), SEO, and social distribution.
  • Experience with HubSpot or a comparable marketing-automation platform for newsletters and lifecycle.
  • Experience with events/conference products, video, or podcasts.
  • A strong interest in the digital asset industry and the intersection of technology and finance.

Bullish US LLC & CoinDesk Inc. are committed to offering competitive compensation and benefits. The anticipated base salary for this position is $190,000 - $220,000 + discretionary annual target bonus + equity. Offered salary will be reflective of job related knowledge, skills and commensurate experience.

Bullish is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are fast evolving and striving towards being a globally-diverse community. With integrity at our core, our success is driven by a talented team of individuals and the different perspectives they are encouraged to bring to work every day.

Category Labs (formerly known as Monad Labs) is a team of systems engineers and researchers on a mission to design and build at the frontier of decentralized technology. We strive to deliver significant improvements over existing blockchain solutions. After raising $225M in Series A funding, led by Paradigm, we are growing our team.

We’re the team behind Monad, a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1. We write the core software that runs it: a parallel-execution EVM, a custom state database, and a BFT consensus client, all developed in the open.

The Role

  • We’re hiring Summer Research Interns to pursue advanced research in mechanism design, cryptoeconomics, distributed systems, programming languages, cryptography, and governance. This list isn’t exhaustive; if you bring a valuable and relevant perspective, we encourage you to apply.

  • This internship offers a rare chance to work at the frontier of decentralized systems: advancing the underlying science and technology while delivering real impact at scale.

  • Research projects will draw on the challenges of building a first-of-its-kind blockchain, as well as new directions that decentralized systems make possible. You’re also welcome to propose your own projects.

  • You’ll learn from Category Labs’ researchers, engineers, and fellow interns, while contributing as an independent and equal peer.

  • Depending on your availability and the needs of the project, the internship can be extended into part-time employment and may lead to future collaborations.

What You’ll Do

  • Conduct novel, rigorous research on the topics above.

  • Contribute to technical publications, including peer-reviewed papers, blog posts, and white papers.

  • Partner with the engineering team to build prototypes, run simulations, and design experiments that test your models and assumptions.

  • Engage with team members and visiting researchers to refine ideas and share insights from your own work.

Past interns have shipped real work (small sample):

  • A Private RPC for Public Blockchains: Introduced write-public ORAM, a new primitive for reading blockchain state without revealing what you read, and built an open-source private RPC that keeps up with Monad’s throughput.

  • Timing Games in Responsive Consensus Protocols: Modeled why validators delay block proposals, and designed dynamic block rewards that make proposing promptly the winning strategy.

  • On the Geographic Incentives of Multiple Concurrent Proposers: Proved how proposers choose where to locate in multi-proposer systems, and when that leads to co-location versus geographic diversity.

Who You Are

  • You’re currently enrolled in a PhD program in computer science, economics, mathematics, the social sciences, or a related field. Exceptional master’s and undergraduate students will also be considered.

  • You’re passionate about decentralized systems and have enough foundational knowledge to hit the ground running.

  • You communicate clearly and can explain complex ideas in simple terms, making research accessible to a broader audience.

  • You have a clear research vision and the drive to pursue innovative ideas aligned with Category Labs’ mission.

  • You’re collaborative, self-motivated, and adaptable, eager to tackle hard problems and pick up new concepts quickly in a fast-paced environment.

Why Work with Us

  • Challenging problems: You’ll work on extremely challenging problems with massive impact. See our Blogs and Publications & Talks for a flavor of the problems we are solving in the real world.

  • Huge opportunity: The Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) standard is ubiquitous, but existing EVM-compatible chains are very slow. Monad’s core innovations offer developers the best of both worlds (portability and performance) and are a game-changer for mass user adoption in crypto.

  • The right team: You’ll be part of a small, exceptional team (engineers and researchers make up 90% of the team).

  • Open by default: Our core software is public on GitHub.

  • Culture: We’re a lean team working together to achieve very ambitious goals. We are united in our culture of collaboration, low ego, and high-quality output. As an early member of our team, you’ll help to shape our culture.

  • Compensation: You’ll receive competitive pay, plus housing support.

  • Resources and growth: We’re well-capitalized, with backing from leading venture funds like Paradigm, Electric Capital, Greenoaks, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures. We keep a lean team, and this is a rare opportunity to join. You’ll learn a lot and grow as our company scales.

How We Use AI

We’re an AI-native team, and we expect researchers to use AI and adapt to the technology as it evolves. A few things we believe:

  • AI is leverage, not a crutch. You must stand behind the correctness and quality of your work (including writing and presentation) even if it was produced with the help of AI.

  • As part of the research process, you must understand the output from AI before sharing it with your collaborators. Any output that you were not able to review must be marked as such.

Internship Details

  • The internship runs roughly 12 weeks, between May 17 and August 30.

  • Residency in New York City is strongly preferred but not required.

  • The anticipated rate for this role is $4,500 per week, plus a $500 per week housing stipend or corporate housing. Pay may vary based on experience and scope.

Application and timeline

Please include, in addition to the application below:

  • Resume/CV

  • Letters of recommendation (1-2 letters, optional but recommended).

    • Recommenders should email their letters of support to recruiting@category.xyz with the "[name of the applicant], Research Intern 2027" in the subject line.

  • For full consideration, please submit applications by December 7, 2026.

Visa & Work Authorization

  • We welcome international applicants and will consider visa and work authorization support on a case-by-case basis. Please note your current status and location in your application so we can discuss options early.

BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our New York, NY office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

  • Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.
  • The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.
  • Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.
  • Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.
  • The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.
  • Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.
  • The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.
  • How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.
  • Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.
  • The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

  • Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.
  • You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.
  • Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.
  • Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.
  • You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.
  • Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.
  • Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.
  • You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

  • Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.
  • Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.
  • Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

  • Competitive base salary, bonus, and stock options
  • 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents
  • Up to 4% 401k company match
  • Paid parental leave, Paid vacation
  • Free commuter/parking pass
  • Free custom lunches and snacks
  • Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs
  • Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

Luxor is a full-stack platform for the Bitcoin mining and digital infrastructure industries. We build software, hardware, financial, and energy solutions that help mining operators improve performance, manage risk, optimize costs, and scale their operations.

Location: Miami, FL or San Francisco, CA, in office. Our Miami office opens in Q1 2027; until then, Miami-based hires work remotely with regular customer travel.
Start: Immediately
Reports to: SVP, Business Development

Every Galaxy campus depends on a controls network that ties cooling, electrical, and monitoring systems together, and it has to behave the same way at the next site as it does at the last one. As Data Center Controls Network Engineer, you will sit within Galaxy’s Pre-Construction team and act as the owner’s technical voice on OT networking, from the point a site is acquired through GMP handoff to construction. About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. About the team

Abuse Control Engineering (ACE) is Stripe’s rapid-response technical defense and control incubator. When urgent abuse vectors emerge, ACE uses real-world attacker telemetry to prototype, test, and deploy software safeguards before vulnerabilities can be exploited at scale.

We partner closely with Fraud, Risk, Abuse Research, and Product Engineering to run rigorous experiments that balance effective risk mitigation with legitimate user activity and conversion. Operating as both a strike team and an incubator, ACE builds automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring and transfers mature controls to long-term product owners across Stripe.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Control Engineer on the ACE team, you will design, prototype, and incubate technical defenses that safeguard Stripe’s financial ecosystem against complex, cross-cutting abuse vectors.

When emerging threat patterns reveal weaknesses in Stripe products, ACE rapidly builds and experiments with technical safeguards. Guided by empirical evidence and Stripe’s Fraud Taxonomy 3.0 (FT3) framework, you will translate threat intelligence into precise technical control requirements, such as API rate limits, step-up challenges, parameter validation, and pre-debit holds.

You will run experiments to evaluate risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, carefully balancing security and product velocity. You will manage controls through a structured incubation lifecycle, build automated regression suites to prevent threats from recurring, and partner with product engineering teams to transfer mature, long-term defenses.

Responsibilities

  • Rapid control prototyping: Design, prototype, and deploy technical controls across API, protocol, and product boundaries to address high-impact abuse vectors.
  • Evidence-based technical requirements: Translate empirical attacker evidence and FT3 threat research from Abuse Research, Fraud, and Security teams into precise technical abuse requirements and control specifications.
  • Control co-design: Collaborate with teams across Stripe to design resilient, secure controls across payments, onboarding, identity, and Connect surfaces.
  • Risk experimentation: Run rigorous experiments and A/B tests to measure risk reduction against the impact on legitimate user conversion, optimizing controls to minimize friction while neutralizing threats.
  • Regression testing: Build comprehensive regression test suites and automated attack simulations with Abuse Research to ensure mitigated abuse vectors do not recur.
  • Stakeholder management: Execute ACE’s incubation model by defining handoff criteria, operational documentation, timelines, and target dates for transferring successful controls to product teams.

The role & why it matters 

We are looking for someone to take ownership of Transaction Monitoring at BCB and shape its next stage. You report to the Head of Financial Crime Operations and you will have real authority over how transaction monitoring works across fiat and crypto, as the first line of defence for the Group.

This is a role for someone who sees a process that could work better and improves it without waiting to be asked.

BCB moves fiat and digital assets 24/7 for some of the largest crypto businesses in the world, through our Client Console, API and BLINC instant settlement network. Monitoring has to keep pace with that volume and speed. We have solid foundations, and we want a leader who will build on them to create a function that is data-led, well documented, measurable and increasingly automated, and that keeps alert and case volumes under control as the business grows.

What you will own

  • The transaction monitoring framework for fiat and crypto across the Group, including rules, scenarios, thresholds, typologies and the documented rationale behind each.
  • Confirm every product, entity and payment flow feeds the monitoring system completely and accurately, including new products before launch.
  • Alert handling end to end: triage, investigation, escalation, case management and closure, with clear SLAs and quality standards, covering transaction monitoring alerts, sanctions and PEP screening hits on customers and counterparties.
  • Backlog and capacity: keep alert and case queues within tolerance, plan rotas and capacity against volume growth, and step in quickly when backlogs build.
  • Oversight of any outsourced or third-party review capacity, including SLA performance, quality and escalation standards.
  • Decisions to escalate internal suspicious activity reports (ISARs) to the MLRO, and the quality of those reports: well reasoned, evidenced and on time, and support to the MLRO in preparing external SARs/STRs, including to the NCA, TRACFIN and FINTRAC. 
  • Rule calibration tuning and effectiveness testing, using data to cut false positives and find the activity current rules miss. Document rationale behind each, with changes approved through BCB’s governance process in partnership with Compliance (2LOD) and the MLRO.
  • Automation of manual, low-judgement, work, whether through vendor tooling, workflow automation, scripting or AI-assisted review.
  • Blockchain analytics as part of monitoring, not a separate step.
  • A quality assurance and quality control framework for the team, with sampling, feedback loops and results reported to governance.
  • Management information for senior leadership and governance forums: volumes, backlog, ageing, conversion rates, quality results, emerging risk.
  • Procedures (SOPs) for the function, kept current and usable by the people doing the work.
  • Leadership of the TM team of over 10 people, working through senior analysts: team structure, hiring, coaching, and performance, and building senior analysts who can make day-to-day decisions without you. Building a robust operating model that increasingly relies upon efficiency, automated workflows and AI over increased headcount.
  • Working relationships with Compliance, Onboarding, Fraud, Product, Engineering and Data, and with regulators and auditors when they review the function. Represent transaction monitoring at governance forums and deputise for the Head of Financial Crime Operations on monitoring matters. 

What success looks like

First 30 days. Review the current rules, alert volumes, backlog, team structure and procedures. Meet the team and key stakeholders. Present a written assessment of what works, what does not and what you will change first, with a sequenced plan and a view on capacity and resourcing .

First 90 days. Any backlog is cleared or on a committed recovery plan. Alerts are consistently worked within SLA. Rules have been reviewed and tuned, with documented rationale for each change and governance approval for each change. At least two manual processes are automated. MI is produced to a regular cadence for senior leadership to review. Every team member has clear objectives and a development plan.

First 3-6 months. Monitoring coverage maps to BCB's risk assessment and product set, including new products before launch. False positive rates are measurably lower with no loss of detection, and investigations are faster. QC and QA results consistently meet targets. The function would pass an internal audit or regulatory review without material findings, and the team runs well without you in every decision, senior analysts own day-to-day case decisions and you have a credible deputy in your absence.

What you bring

  • Five or more years in transaction monitoring or financial crime investigations, with at least two in a lead or management role.
  • Experience in payments, e-money, banking or crypto. Experience across both fiat and crypto is a strong advantage.
  • A track record of improving a monitoring function: you can describe a rule set you rebuilt, a backlog you cleared or a process you automated, and the numbers before and after.
  • Experience of workforce and capacity planning, QA/QC frameworks and managing operational SLAs, including oversight of outsourced review capacity. 
  • Hands-on knowledge of rule design, threshold calibration and effectiveness testing.
  • Sound judgement on suspicion and SAR decisions, and the ability to teach that judgement to others.
  • Working knowledge of UK AML requirements, including the MLRs and JMLSG guidance, and of sanctions regimes (UK, EU, OFAC, UN) and PEP screening. Some exposure to EU requirements. Experience of France’s ACPR or AMF and reporting to TRACFIN, reporting to FINTRAC in Canada and an understanding of the FIU reporting regimes in UAE and Switzerland is an advantage.
  • Comfort with data. You can query it, interpret it and make decisions from it. SQL or Python is a plus.
  • Experience with blockchain analytics tools such as Chainalysis, Elliptic or TRM.
  • A clear view on where automation and AI help in monitoring, and where they need human oversight.
  • Clear and precise written English. Your case notes, SOPs and MI are easy to follow and hard to misread.

How you work

You are direct and decisive. You make a call, explain it and own the outcome. You question rules and processes that exist only because they always have. You prefer fixing root causes over adding headcount. Can produce MI such as cost per alert and capacity forecasting against volume growth. You build trust with the team by being in the detail with them, and with senior stakeholders by telling them plainly what the risk is. You develop your senior analysts so decisions do not all route through you.

Business Insights & Strategy

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. About the team

Specialist Solutions Architects (SSAs) are domain experts aligned to Stripe’s solutions and the customer buying centers they serve. We combine deep product and industry expertise with an understanding of our customers’ most complex business and technical challenges.

The SSA team partners with specialist sellers and the broader pre-sales organization to shape strategic opportunities, develop pipeline, improve revenue attainment, and turn Stripe’s product capabilities into measurable customer outcomes. We also bring field insights to Product and Engineering, helping influence Stripe’s roadmap and go-to-market strategy.

Stripe's Revenue Suite helps businesses monetize however their customers want to buy: subscription, usage-based, or hybrid pricing. As monetization models get more complex and pricing becomes something companies iterate on continuously rather than set once, this team sits at the center of how Stripe helps businesses price, bill, recognize, and report on revenue.

What you’ll do

As Global Head of Specialist Solutions Architecture for Revenue, you will lead the global strategy, execution, and growth of the SSA organization supporting Stripe's full Revenue Suite: Stripe Billing and Metronome together. You will define how Stripe engages customers across the entire monetization-to-revenue-reporting lifecycle, including subscription management, usage-based and hybrid billing, invoicing, tax, revenue recognition, and analytics, from initial business and technical discovery through solution design, adoption, value realization, and expansion.

This is a second line leadership role. You will manage a mix of regional managers, each leading their own team of specialist architects, along with a small number of senior individual contributors reporting to you directly. You will build and develop this multi-layered organization and create the operating model, playbooks, and cross-functional partnerships needed to scale it worldwide. Working closely with Sales, Marketing, Alliances, Professional Services, Support, Product, and Engineering, you will help customers modernize their revenue infrastructure while accelerating adoption and growth for Stripe's Revenue Suite across every region we operate in.

This is an opportunity to shape a global function at an important point in Stripe's expansion beyond payments. You will connect deep technical expertise to customer value and commercial outcomes while ensuring that customer needs from every region influence Stripe's global product and go-to-market direction.

Responsibilities

  • Own and execute the global technical sales strategy for Stripe's Revenue Suite, aligning specialist coverage, priorities, and investments with growth opportunities across AMER, EMEA, and APAC
  • Recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing organization of regional managers and senior individual contributors, establishing clear expectations for technical excellence, customer impact, and commercial contribution
  • Coach and develop your managers directly, building their leadership capability so they can in turn grow strong specialist architects on their own teams
  • Partner with Sales leadership to prioritize resources, shape account strategies, and improve the progression and conversion of complex opportunities
  • Establish repeatable engagement models, playbooks, reference architectures, and execution standards across the monetization-to-revenue-reporting lifecycle, including subscription management, usage-based and hybrid billing, invoicing, tax, revenue recognition, and analytics
  • Advise executives, developers, architects, finance leaders, and other decision-makers on modernizing their monetization and revenue-management architectures
  • Guide strategic customers from business and technical discovery through solution design, validation, adoption, value realization, and expansion
  • Translate recurring customer needs, market signals, and deal friction into actionable insights that influence Product and Engineering priorities
  • Represent the Revenue SSA organization in global leadership forums, providing clear perspectives on performance, capacity, risks, customer needs, and growth opportunities
  • Shape the Revenue Suite go-to-market approach across every region, accounting for regional regulatory requirements, business models, and market-specific billing practices
  • Build strong collaboration and knowledge-sharing mechanisms across regional and global teams to improve consistency, reuse, and execution quality
  • Advance Stripe's external thought leadership through executive briefings, industry events, white papers, and reference architectures focused on billing, monetization, tax automation, and revenue management

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 15+ years of experience in technical sales, solutions architecture, solution consulting, or another customer-facing technical role in enterprise technology
  • 10+ years of experience building and scaling pre-sales or solutions architecture teams, including hiring, managing, coaching, and developing senior individual contributors 
  • Experience managing managers, with a track record of developing people leaders and running a multi-layered organization
  • Demonstrated success partnering with sales leaders on complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise opportunities and connecting technical strategy to commercial outcomes
  • Deep understanding of modern monetization models, including subscription, usage-based, and hybrid pricing, and how businesses increasingly treat pricing as something to iterate on continuously rather than set once, and how that shapes billing, invoicing, and revenue-management requirements
  • Strong technical background with a solid understanding of APIs, distributed systems, and modern software development practices
  • Experience operating across global markets, with an ability to adapt leadership and go-to-market approaches across different regions and cultures
  • Strong executive communication, relationship-building, and cross-functional leadership skills
  • Ability to communicate complex business and technical concepts clearly to audiences ranging from developers and architects to finance leaders and C-level executives
  • Willingness to travel up to 30% of the time

Preferred qualifications

  • Working knowledge of the full revenue management lifecycle: recurring and usage-based billing, subscription management, invoicing, tax automation (sales tax and VAT), revenue recognition, financial/custom reporting, and the data pipelines that feed them
  • Experience designing or advising on complex enterprise architectures and integrations involving financial or revenue-management systems, including configure-price-quote, order-to-cash, revenue recognition, and ERP systems
  • Experience with usage-based or consumption billing platforms and the metering, pricing, and invoicing architectures they require
  • Experience building or scaling a global technical go-to-market function during a period of rapid product or organizational growth
  • A track record of translating field insights into meaningful product, engineering, or go-to-market changes
  • Experience developing executive-facing thought leadership, reference architectures, or industry-specific solution strategies
  • Familiarity with the regulatory and commercial considerations that affect billing, tax, and revenue management across AMER, EMEA, and APAC

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime.   • Clarity and polish in writing and presentations

  • Experience with planning cycles (monthly, quarterly, annual)

  • Comfort with working independently and proactively driving outcomes

  • Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or Business Administration preferred; MBA a plus

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. About the role

As Circle expands the customers and payment methods it serves, our fraud exposure grows and changes. We rely on conservative limits and third-party models today, and we are building our own.


As a Senior Data Scientist on Fraud Analytics, you will own the prediction side of our fraud loop. You will turn labels into features and models, measure their accuracy, and shift Circle from vendor scores to in-house models. You will work with Fraud Strategy, Fraud Operations, Risk Engineering, and Compliance.


What you’ll do

  • Build and evaluate fraud models for onboarding, login, account changes, and money movement. Target risks include account takeover, scams, money mules, and stolen and synthetic identity.
  • Evaluate third-party risk signals and design the path from vendor models to Circle models, from shadow mode to production.
  • Define the label taxonomy and data requirements with Fraud Operations and Risk Engineering, so every event, decision, and outcome becomes training data. This includes the fraud we miss.
  • Design holdout and exploration sampling to measure false negatives and the rate at which we wrongly block good customers.
  • Track fraud rate, dispute rate, fraud loss rate, and precision across customer segments. Help set thresholds against an agreed loss budget.
  • Work with Fraud Strategy to tune thresholds and rules and respond to emerging attacks.
  • Backtest, monitor drift, and retrain models on Circle’s fraud platform.
  • Help build AI agent workflows for transaction review, fraud-ring analysis, and rule drafting, and evaluate their accuracy against human labels.

Core Requirements

  • 5+ years in data science or applied ML on fraud, risk, or financial crime
  • Advanced Python and SQL, and experience with XGBoost, LightGBM, or similar
  • Experience building models with sparse, delayed, or biased labels, including cold start, reject inference, and chargeback lag
  • Strong statistics: anomaly detection, graph or network methods, experimentation, and threshold optimization
  • Experience taking models to production and monitoring them
  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical partners
  • Comfort working through ambiguity and limited historical data

Preferred Requirements

  • Fintech, payments, crypto, or card fraud experience, including chargebacks and disputes
  • Experience with device intelligence, behavioral signals, or consortium data
